title: An orchestrator whose main checkout another session uses moves to its own worktree before its first claim, and land and dispatch accept worker worktrees under it
goal: SP-befc6yqr: another session left untracked sprint files in the shared main checkout, so land refused the clean tree; the orchestrator moved to a linked worktree, where land refused workers made under the main checkout's .claude/worktrees (they had to be moved with git worktree move) and selfcheck's checkout check fails for a linked worktree. The kb-sprint run step names how an orchestrator that finds foreign files in its checkout moves (a linked worktree it starts from, or a clone), selfcheck tells that case from a linked worktree whose workers land fine, and land names the worktree it expects.

run: import os,pathlib,subprocess,sys,tempfile;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_land,bl_dispatch;d=os.path.realpath(tempfile.mkdtemp());m=d+'/main';g=lambda*a:subprocess.run(['git','-C',m,*a],check=True,capture_output=True);subprocess.run(['git','init','-q',m],check=True);g('-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@e','commit','-q','--allow-empty','-m','x');g('worktree','add','-q',d+'/linked','-b','l');w=m+'/.claude/worktrees/agent-ST-aaaaaaaa';g('worktree','add','-q',w,'-b','work/ST-aaaaaaaa');r=bl_land.release_worker_worktree(d+'/linked',pathlib.Path(w),None,branch='work/ST-aaaaaaaa');t={str(p) for p in bl_land.worker_dirs(d+'/linked')};p=str(bl_dispatch.worktree_path(d+'/linked','ST-aaaaaaaa').parent);ok=r is None and p in t;print('land releases a main checkout worker and dispatch workers of a linked worktree stay accepted:',ok,r);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: Which land operations accept a worker worktree under the main checkout's .claude/worktrees when the orchestrator runs in a linked worktree: land of one item's branch only, or every operation that reads worker_dirs (tidy and close too)?
options: land of one item's branch only: release_worker_worktree accepts it; tidy and close keep the clone's own directory
every operation that reads worker_dirs: land, tidy and close
gates.recommendation: land of one item's branch only: release_worker_worktree accepts it; tidy and close keep the clone's own directory
gates.answer: land of one item's branch only: release_worker_worktree accepts it; tidy and close keep the clone's own directory

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 12 of 13, "Planning rules 2: plan-time warnings and probes"); the triage reviewer found it serves the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test F2: a content sprint from the research queue lands on headless Sonnet workers. Premise: for a clone that is a linked worktree, bl_land.worker_dirs names only its own .claude/worktrees, selfcheck's checkout check fails it, and the run step 2 does not name the move (the story's check and its tasks' checks). Run at plan 2026-10-10: all four exit 1 on the base, so the premise reproduces. Split into tasks TK-lwihhcmj (land), TK-wddzrzod (selfcheck) and TK-tbbknjul (the skill), run in that order. dispatch makes its worktree under the toplevel of the clone it runs in, which land accepts, so the story's check pins that and no dispatch task is planned. The earlier check, backlog.py check, passed on the base and proved nothing, so it was replaced.
